<!--
apa-twocolumn asks for a float to be set across both columns of a journal
article. A float written as a markdown image carries the attribute on the
image and quarto hands it to the float it builds; a float written as a code
chunk carries it on the cell div instead, and the float inside that div never
saw it, so a wide figure was set inside one column and ran over the text
beside it.

Base R draws the figure. The point is which environment the float is written
into, not the picture.

A successful run produces:

  - figure* for both wide figures, the one written as an image and the one
    written as a chunk, and table* for the wide table;
  - figure for the narrow figure, which asked for nothing and should be set
    in its column like any other;
  - one note for each float, inside the float rather than left behind in the
    column it was written in.
-->

# Method

See @fig-wideimage, @fig-widechunk, @fig-narrow and @tbl-widechunk.

![A wide figure written as a markdown image.](sampleimage.png){#fig-wideimage apa-twocolumn="true" apa-note="A note on the wide image."}

```{r}
#| label: fig-widechunk
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "A wide figure written as a code chunk."
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-alt: A line.
#| apa-twocolumn: true
#| apa-note: "A note on the wide chunk."
plot(1:10, type = "l", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-narrow
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "A narrow figure written as a code chunk."
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-alt: Another line.
#| apa-note: "A note on the narrow chunk."
plot(10:1, type = "l", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-widechunk
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "A wide table written as a code chunk."
#| apa-twocolumn: true
#| apa-note: "A note on the wide table."
knitr::kable(data.frame(a = 1:2, b = 3:4))
```
